'''Zvezdelina Entcheva Stankova''' ({{langx|bg|Звезделина Енчева Станкова}}; born 15 September 1969) is a Bulgarian and American mathematician who is a teaching professor of mathematics at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], the founder of the <span class="anchor" id="BMC"></span>'''Berkeley Math Circle''', and an expert in the [[Enumerative combinatorics|combinatorial enumeration]] of [[Permutation pattern|permutations with forbidden patterns]].<ref name="proof">{{citation |url=http://www.proofschool.org/stankova/ |title=Zvezdelina Stankova |publisher=[[Proof School]] |access-date=2016-02-03 |archive-date=2018-12-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181209231245/http://www.proofschool.org/stankova |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{citation |title=Zvezdelina Stankova {{!}} Department of Mathematics |url=https://math.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/zvezdelina-stankova |access-date=2026-08-20 |website=math.berkeley.edu}}</ref> 

==Early life==
Stankova was born in [[Ruse, Bulgaria|Ruse]], Bulgaria (then the [[People's Republic of Bulgaria]]).<ref name="whiz"/> She began attending the Ruse [[math circle]] as a fifth grader, the same year she learned to solve the [[Rubik's Cube]]<ref name="weld">{{citation|url=http://www.themonthly.com/feature1404.html|magazine=[[The East Bay Monthly]]|first=Sarah|last=Weld|date=April 2014|title=Proving Their Passion: The Berkeley Math Circle gives math kids a place to find solutions—together|access-date=2016-02-02|archive-date=2019-02-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190209232529/http://www.themonthly.com/feature1404.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> and began winning regional mathematics competitions.<ref name="proof"/> She later wrote of this experience that "if I was not a member of Ruse SMC [Students Mathematical Circle] I would not be able to make such profound achievements in mathematics".<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.math.bas.bg/talents/en/prep/RSMC.pdf|title=Ruse Students Mathematical Circle|publisher=Institute of Mathematics and Informatics, [[Bulgarian Academy of Sciences]]|access-date=2016-02-02}}.</ref> She became a student at an elite English-language high school, and competed on the Bulgarian team in the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]]s in 1987 and 1988, earning silver medals both times.<ref name="whiz"/><ref>{{citation|url=https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=1599|title=Participant record: Zvezdelina Stankova|publisher=[[International Mathematical Olympiad]]|access-date=2016-02-02}}.</ref> She entered [[Sofia University]] but in 1989, as the [[Iron Curtain]] was falling, became one of 15 Bulgarian students selected to travel to the US to complete their studies.<ref name="whiz">{{citation|url=http://articles.philly.com/1991-10-23/news/25814612_1_math-talent-sofia-university-algebra |title=Bulgarian Math Whiz Wows 'Em: Zvezdelina Stankova Already Is Joining The Ranks Of Top Mathematicians. "She's A Genius," Says Bryn Mawr's Head Of Math|first=Ralph|last=Vigoda|date=October 23, 1991|newspaper=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222080713/http://articles.philly.com/1991-10-23/news/25814612_1_math-talent-sofia-university-algebra|archive-date=December 22, 2015}}.</ref>

Stankova studied at [[Bryn Mawr College]], completing bachelor's and master's degrees there in 1992,<ref name="mills">{{citation|url=http://www.mills.edu/academics/faculty/math/stankova/stankova.php|title=Zvezdelina Stankova|work=Mathematics Faculty and Staff|publisher=Mills College|access-date=2016-02-01}}.</ref> with [[Rhonda Hughes]] as a faculty mentor.<ref name="alumnews">{{citation|url=http://alumnews.blogs.brynmawr.edu/2011/04/06/zvezdelina-stankova-%E2%80%9992-carries-on-a-bryn-mawr-tradition-excellent-teaching-in-mathematics/|title=Zvezdelina Stankova '92 Carries on a Bryn Mawr Tradition: Excellent Teaching in Mathematics|date=April 6, 2011|first=Katherine|last=Bakke|work=Meaningful Contributions|publisher=Bryn Mawr College}}.</ref> While an undergraduate, she participated in a summer research program with [[Joseph Gallian]] at the [[University of Minnesota Duluth]], which began her interest in [[permutation pattern]]s.<ref name="schafer"/> Next, she went to [[Harvard University]] for her doctoral studies and earned a Ph.D. there in 1997; her dissertation, entitled ''Moduli of Trigonal Curves'', was supervised by [[Joe Harris (mathematician)|Joe Harris]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=18792}}</ref> She also earned a Massachusetts [[Certified teacher|teaching credential]] in 1997 and California's equivalent credential in 1998.<ref name="cv" /> 

==Career==
Stankova joined the [[Mills College]] faculty in 1999, following a postdoctoral fellowship at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name="cv" /><ref name=":0">{{citation |date=Fall 2016 |title=Mathematics + Berkeley Fall 2016 |url=https://math.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/bulk_7/Newsletter2016_0.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240101060022/https://math.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/bulk_7/Newsletter2016_0.pdf |archive-date=2024-01-01}}</ref> She remained on the Mills faculty until 2016, but began in 2002 also teaching one course per year at Berkeley as a visiting professor.<ref name="haimo">{{citation|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/prize-booklet-2011.pdf|work=January 2011 Prizes and Awards|date=January 7, 2011|publisher=American Mathematical Society|title=Haimo Award Citation: Zvezdelina Stankova|page=4|access-date=February 2, 2016|archive-date=March 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304000923/http://www.ams.org/profession/prize-booklet-2011.pdf|url-status=dead}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|url=https://math.berkeley.edu/~stankova/|title=Stankova's home page at Berkeley|access-date=2016-02-02}}.</ref><ref name=":0" /> She joined Berkeley's mathematics department full-time in 2016, as a teaching professor.<ref name=":0" /> 

Parallel to her work in higher education, Stankova has taught middle and high school students. She founded the Berkeley [[Math circle|Math Circle]], an after-school math enrichment program, and co-founded the Bay Area Mathematical Olympiad, both in 1998.<ref name="weld" /><ref name="alumnews" /><ref>{{citation|title=Circle in a Box|volume=2|series=MSRI mathematical circles library|publisher=Mathematical Sciences Research Institute and American Mathematical Society|first=Sam|last=Vandervelde|year=2009|isbn=9780821847527|pages=4, 34|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wkZ-AwAAQBAJ&pg=PA4}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|url=http://www.1011now.com/home/headlines/Moms-Everyday-Making-Math-Fun-228617341.html|title=Moms Everyday: Making Math Fun|date=October 21, 2013|first=Melanie|last=Bloom|publisher=[[KOLN|10/11]]|access-date=February 2, 2016|archive-date=May 20, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160520184419/http://www.1011now.com/home/headlines/Moms-Everyday-Making-Math-Fun-228617341.html|url-status=dead}}.</ref><ref name="ucb">{{citation|url=http://www.berkeley.edu/news/media/releases/99legacy/2-10-1999.html|title=UC Berkeley mathematicians feed the minds of young local math whizzes|first=Tamara|last=Keith|date=February 10, 1999|publisher=[[University of California, Berkeley]]}}.</ref> From 1998 to 2004, she coached the US [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] team.<ref name="alumnews" /><ref name="abc7" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2004-08-13 |title=MathFest 2004: PRIZES and AWARDS |url=https://maa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/PRZBKmathfest2004.pdf |url-status=live}}</ref> In 2016, she founded Math Taught the Right Way, a Berkeley-based program that adapts Bulgarian middle- and high-school mathematics curricula for American students.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stankova |first=Zvezdelina |date=2018-09-25 |title=1145-M5-2925 |url=https://www.jointmathematicsmeetings.org/amsmtgs/2217_abstracts/1145-m5-2925.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211202073510/https://jointmathematicsmeetings.org/amsmtgs/2217_abstracts/1145-m5-2925.pdf |archive-date=2021-12-02}}</ref> Since 2014, she has been president of the United Math Circles Foundation, the nonprofit umbrella organization of the Berkeley Math Circle.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Roberts |first=Andrea Suozzo, Alec Glassford, Ash Ngu, Brandon |date=2013-05-09 |title=United Math Circles Foundation - Nonprofit Explorer |url=https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/463636266 |access-date=2026-08-20 |website=ProPublica |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=United Math Circles Foundation — Form 990 financials, salaries & grants (EIN 46-3636266) {{!}} philanthropy.org |url=https://philanthropy.org/990/report/463636266/united-math-circles-foundation |access-date=2026-08-20 |website=990 Scout |language=en}}</ref> She has also served on the advisory board of the [[Proof School]] in San Francisco.<ref name="proof" />

Since June 2026, Stankova has been a prominent advocate for reforms in undergraduate admissions. She co-authored an open letter, signed by thousands of UC faculty members, urging the university to reinstate an admissions testing policy it had rescinded in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Burke |first=Michael |title=UC freshmen increasingly are not ready for college math. Some professors want to require the SAT again |url=https://edsource.org/2026/reinstate-sat-uc-admissions/760013 |access-date=2026-08-20 |website=EdSource |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rony |first=Alexander |date=2026-06-11 |title=UC Berkeley mathematicians reignite national conversation on college admissions and SAT/ACT scores |url=https://ls.berkeley.edu/news/uc-berkeley-mathematicians-reignite-national-conversation-college-admissions-and-satact-scores |access-date=2026-08-20 |website=Letters & Science |language=en}}</ref> She has represented the letter's stance in news media and before the UC Board of Regents.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peralta |first=Eyder |date=2026-06-06 |title=UC Berkeley professor Zvezdelina Stankova explains push to reinstate standardized exams - VPM |url=https://www.vpm.org/npr-news/2026-06-06/uc-berkeley-professor-zvezdelina-stankova-explains-push-to-reinstate-standardized-exams/ |access-date=2026-08-20 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-08-15 |title=Opinion: I teach calculus at Berkeley. Some of my students can’t do middle school math |url=https://sfstandard.com/opinion/2026/08/15/uc-berkeley-sat-test-blind-admissions-math-scores/ |access-date=2026-08-20 |website=The San Francisco Standard |language=en}}</ref> She drew criticism in August 2026 following reports she had used [[generative AI]] to edit her public statements.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=Francis Luo {{!}} |date=2026-08-18 |title=UC Berkeley professor admits to using AI in op-ed calling out students’ lack of math proficiency |url=https://www.dailycal.org/news/campus/uc-berkeley-professor-admits-to-using-ai-in-op-ed-calling-out-students-lack-of/article_be1360f7-6e2a-42f6-ae76-f05d8cee74c4.html |access-date=2026-08-20 |website=Daily Cal {{!}} Berkeley news |language=en}}</ref><ref name="guard-19aug2026">{{citation |last1=Sullivan |first1=Sophie |title=UC Berkeley professor admits to using AI to edit op-ed on students' math skills |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/19/uc-berkeley-professor-ai |access-date=August 19, 2026 |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=August 19, 2026}}</ref> She subsequently discussed AI, including its utility and danger for higher education, during a live interview with [[Greta Van Susteren|Greta van Susteren]].<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gBW2l1DOgAc |title=Is America First Dead In Our Schools? {{!}} Greta Wire |date=2026-08-21 |last=Newsmax |access-date=2026-08-21 |via=YouTube}}</ref>  

==Contributions==
In the theory of [[permutation pattern]]s, Stankova is known for proving that the permutations with the forbidden pattern 1342 are equinumerous with the permutations with forbidden pattern 2413, an important step in the enumeration of permutations avoiding a pattern of length 4.<ref name="schafer"/><ref name="bona">{{citation|title=Combinatorics of Permutations|edition=2nd|series=Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications|first=Miklos|last=Bona|publisher=CRC Press|year=2012|isbn=9781439850527|pages=154–155|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Y3nRBQAAQBAJ&pg=PA154}}.</ref>

The Berkeley Math Circle, which Stankova founded, was only the second math circle in the US (after one in Boston); following its success, over 100 other circles have been created,<ref name="weld"/> and Stankova has assisted in the formation of many of them.<ref name="haimo"/>

Since 2013, Stankova has been featured in several videos on the mathematics-themed [[YouTube]] channel "[[Numberphile]]".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Zvezdelina Stankova on Numberphile |url=http://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLt5AfwLFPxWIbAPK1oJgRIpe0sWiPKkQ4 |access-date=2026-08-21 |website=YouTube |language=en}}</ref>

==Publications==
With Tom Rike, she is co-editor of two books about her work with the Berkeley Math Circle, ''A Decade of the Berkeley Math Circle: The American Experience'' (Vol. I, 2008, Vol. II, 2014).<ref>{{citation|title=MSRI Mathematical Circles Library|url=https://www.mathcircles.org/content/math-circle-library|publisher=National Association of Math Circles|access-date=2016-02-01|archive-date=2017-06-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170606193839/http://www.mathcircles.org/content/math-circle-library|url-status=dead}}.</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Stankova received the [[Alice T. Schafer Prize]] in 1992, while an undergraduate.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=September 1992 |title=FOCUS: The Newsletter of the Mathematical Association of America |url=https://old.maa.org/sites/default/files/pdf/pubs/focus/past_issues/FOCUS_12_4.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251211051230/https://old.maa.org/sites/default/files/pdf/pubs/focus/past_issues/FOCUS_12_4.pdf |archive-date=2025-12-11}}</ref> Awarded by the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]], the prize recognized her research in combinatorics and her [[American Mathematical Society]] paper on forbidden sequences, work her advisor called "strikingly original."<ref name="schafer">{{citation|url=http://www.awm-math.org/schaferprize/1992.html|publisher=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]]|title=Third Annual Alice T. Schafer Prize|date=July 1992|access-date=2016-02-02|archive-date=2020-03-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200330051715/http://www.awm-math.org/schaferprize/1992.html|url-status=dead}}.</ref><ref name="haimo"/><ref name=":2" /> 

For her teaching, Stankova received the [[Mathematical Association of America]]'s award for early-career teaching, the [[Henry L. Alder Award]], in 2004.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Henry L. Alder Award – Mathematical Association of America |url=https://maa.org/henry-l-alder-award/ |access-date=2026-08-21 |language=en-US}}</ref> Among that award's first two recipients, she was credited with "doubling the number of mathematics majors at Mills College."<ref name=":1" /> 

She then received, in 2011, the [[Mathematical Association of America]]'s most competitive award for teaching: the [[Deborah and Franklin Haimo Awards for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics|Deborah and Franklin Tepper Haimo Award]].<ref name="alumnews" /><ref name="haimo" /><ref name="abc7">{{citation|url=http://abc7news.com/archive/7981841/|first=Lyanne|last=Melendez|date=February 25, 2011|title=Mills College professor wins highest math award|publisher=ABC7 News}}.</ref>
The award recognized "her teaching ability, her enthusiasm for mathematics, and her capacity to dramatically change [students'] attitudes toward mathematics and their perceptions of their own mathematical abilities."<ref name="haimo" /> 

Citing student reviews, [[The Princeton Review|Princeton Review]] included Stankova in its 2012 guide, "The Best 300 Professors."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-05-01 |title=Prof. John Majewski on Princeton Review’s “Best 300 Professors” list. – Department of History, UC Santa Barbara |url=https://www.history.ucsb.edu/2012/05/01/prof-john-majewski-on-princeton-reviews-best-300-professors-list/ |access-date=2026-08-21 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=Fall 2012 |title=Mathematics + Berkeley: Fall 2012 |url=https://math.berkeley.edu/sites/default/files/bulk_5/Fall2012.pdf}}</ref> Berkeley students selected Stankova, during her first full year teaching there, to receive the Mathematics Undergraduate Student Association's Distinguished Teaching & Service Award in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mathematics Undergraduate Student Association |url=https://math.berkeley.edu/~musa/teaching_award.html |access-date=2026-08-21 |website=math.berkeley.edu}}</ref> 

From 2009 to 2012 she was the Frederick A. Rice Professor of Mathematics at Mills College.<ref name="cv">{{citation|url=http://www.mills.edu/academics/faculty/math/stankova/ZStankova_cv.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae: Zvezdelina Stankova|access-date=2016-02-01|last=Stankova|first=Zvezdelina|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160202123105/http://www.mills.edu/academics/faculty/math/stankova/ZStankova_cv.pdf|archive-date=2016-02-02|url-status=dead}}</ref>
